findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The PPHQN5 ticket and spec match the C7HCN7 recovery proposal. They limit the work to observation only. They keep certification, closing integration, shared gates, history edits and paid or live runs out of scope. They also hold the 14-block/37-case and 33-deferral counts apart. Each Rule fails closed. The caller cannot substitute a ticket, command, report, filter or success flag. Only a complete passing run of every required assertion, including parameter rows, can succeed. Altered, wrong-purpose or incomplete records refuse. Retries keep earlier attempts. Changed inputs remove current success but leave history readable. The ticket file is projected field by field rather than exempted as a whole. Observations grant no certification or completion. Design details are named as planning obligations, so implementers are not left to guess them. I found nothing that would let a partial, stale or forged result verify as current success. The remaining issues are ambiguities that would fail closed, so they are warnings.

R1 and R3/R4 may conflict on retries. R1 refuses any run with dirty product or execution inputs before execution. R4 allows audit-only output writes, but only when checking whether an observation is still current. If retained attempt records are written inside the repository (for example, under the ticket directory), a failed first attempt can make the tree dirty. Under R1 the next retry would then refuse, which defeats R3's promise that a retry creates another attempt. This fails closed, so no false success results. Still, planning should state whether retained records live outside the candidate's inputs or whether R1's dirty check uses the same audit-only projection as R4.

R2 says the fixed mapping covers all 37 delivery cases. It also says an unsupported case produces a named refusal until its mapping can be reviewed. The Known facts show only that the tests currently pass, not that every case maps to a named assertion. If any case turns out to be unsupported, the observer can never produce a successful observation, and the M1 outcome becomes unreachable without a separate mapping review. That outcome is correct fail-closed behavior. Make it explicit so 'covers all 37' is not read as an already-established fact.

The ticket scope and R3 promise to reject 'tampered evidence' through authentication. The Assumptions, however, trust the local user and host, and authentication uses existing local keys. Authentication therefore detects accidental or out-of-band changes, not a trusted local actor who re-signs records. This is within the accepted trust boundary. The observation's stated execution-evidence-only meaning should still avoid implying stronger protection when a later certification step consumes it.

R1 says the observer binds 'the current committed candidate at request start' but does not say how that candidate is chosen (checkout HEAD versus an explicit commit). Exact CLI syntax is deferred to planning. Planning should still confirm that choosing the candidate cannot become a way to substitute a ticket or scope, and that the candidate must stay a descendant of, or match, the reviewed contract version.
